1. ---
2. name: scan-agentic-app-perf
3. description: |
4.   Scan a .NET agentic application (MAF; Aspire/Foundry optional) across seven perf/cost/reliability categories — topology, tool inventory, message history, prompt weight, parallelism, OTel coverage, per-agent model assignment. Writes .copilot/perf-reports/scan.md (overwritten each run) with severity-tagged findings (critical/warn/info), file:line citations, evidence, and next actions routing into configure-agentic-perf-rules or setup-maf-evals. WHEN: user asks "why is my agent slow", "scan/audit my agentic app", "find perf issues", "is my topology too complex", or just changed a topology. NOT-WHEN: install always-on rules (use configure-agentic-perf-rules), wire evaluations (use setup-maf-evals); not for non-agentic .NET apps. Read-only. Supported topologies: Aspire AppHost, plain console, ASP.NET Core, worker service (Aspire-specific checks such as the AppHost-only model literal apply only when an AppHost is detected). INVOKES: scripts/Detect-{Topology,OtelCoverage,ModelLiterals}.ps1 (pwsh 7+).
5. ---
6. 
7. # scan-agentic-app-perf
8. 
9. Run a structured audit of a .NET agentic application and produce a single
10. Markdown report listing the perf, cost, and reliability issues that matter,
11. each with a concrete next action.
12. 
13. This skill is **read-only**. It never edits source. The output is a report file
14. plus a short chat summary of top findings.
15. 
16. ## When to Use
17. 
18. - The user asks "why is my agent slow", "scan my agentic app", "audit my
19.   agentic app", "find perf issues", or "is my topology too complex".
20. - The user has just modified an agent topology (added an agent, added a
21.   handoff edge, swapped a model, added tools) and wants a sanity check
22.   before merging.
23. - A coding agent is about to make a non-trivial change to a `.NET`
24.   agentic app and wants the current perf/cost baseline to compare
25.   against post-change.
26. 
27. ## When Not to Use
28. 
29. - The user wants to install **always-on** rules so future agent work
30.   surfaces perf concerns by default — use `configure-agentic-perf-rules`.
31. - The user wants to wire **runtime** measurement (latency, tokens,
32.   cost, quality scores) into the project — use `setup-maf-evals`.
33. - The project is not a .NET agentic app — use `optimizing-dotnet-performance`
34.   for general .NET performance guidance.
35. - The user wants the skill to **fix** the findings, not just report
36.   them — this skill is read-only by design; route fixes through
37.   `configure-agentic-perf-rules` (for guard-rails) or normal coding
38.   agent work (for code changes).
39. 
40. ## Supported topologies
41. 
42. The skill targets any .NET project using Microsoft Agent Framework
43. (`Microsoft.Agents.AI`), regardless of how it's hosted:
44. 
45. - **Aspire AppHost** (`*.AppHost.csproj` orchestrating agent services) — the most
46.   common shape; enables AppHost-specific checks such as the "model literal lives
47.   only in the AppHost" check.
48. - **File-based AppHost** (.NET 10) — a single `apphost.cs` (or similarly named
49.   `.cs`) that carries `#:sdk Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` / `#:package` directives and a
50.   `DistributedApplication.CreateBuilder(...)` call, run via `dotnet run apphost.cs`
51.   with **no** `.csproj`/`.sln`. Detected by parsing source text (see step 1), so
52.   the same checks and detection scripts apply.
53. - **Plain console / worker service** — `Microsoft.Agents.AI` registered directly
54.   against an OpenAI or Foundry client without an Aspire AppHost.
55. - **ASP.NET Core minimal API** — agents registered via the same DI patterns.
56. 
57. AppHost-specific checks (those that depend on `*.AppHost.csproj` being present)
58. are silently skipped when no AppHost is detected. All other checks (topology,
59. tool inventory, message history, prompt weight, parallelism, OTel coverage,
60. per-agent model assignment) apply to every topology.
61. 
62. ## Workflow
63. 
64. > **Execution discipline — the user asked a question; answer it in chat.**
65. > - **Your chat response is the primary deliverable.** The user asked you to
66. >   audit their app; they read your answer in the chat, not a file on disk. Your
67. >   final message **must** present the findings (see step 5) — total counts plus
68. >   the top findings with file:line and next action. `scan.md` is a persisted
69. >   copy of that same analysis, not a substitute for it. A run that writes the
70. >   file but ends with an empty or one-line chat message has failed the user.
71. > - **Analyze first, then write both.** Inspect the sources, reason about the
72. >   findings, then (a) present them in chat and (b) persist the same findings to
73. >   `.copilot/perf-reports/scan.md`. Do not open an empty report file up front
74. >   and treat filling it as the goal — that starves the chat answer. Both the
75. >   chat summary and the file are required; the chat summary is the last thing
76. >   you do.
77. > - **Anchor on what the user asked.** If the prompt names a concern
78. >   (topology / "too complex", history / "slow on multi-turn", cost / prompt
79. >   weight, observability / OTel), **lead both the chat answer and the report
80. >   with that category** — never bury it under an unrelated one. Still run the
81. >   full seven-category sweep, but the user's stated problem is the headline.
82. > - **Stay lean; don't over-tool.** On a small app (a handful of source files)
83. >   **read each source file once, skip the detection scripts, and open no
84. >   reference docs.** The PowerShell detectors and per-category reference docs are
85. >   accelerators for large codebases, not a mandatory gauntlet; running them on a
86. >   tiny fixture just burns your turn budget and adds nothing a direct read
87. >   doesn't already give you. Concretely, for an app of ~5 files or fewer, aim to
88. >   finish inventory + all seven categories in **well under ~10 tool calls** —
89. >   read the files, reason, answer. Do not re-open a file you already read, never
90. >   pre-read all seven reference docs, and open one only to confirm a specific
91. >   candidate finding you can't resolve from the source.
92. 
93. ### 1. Inventory the app
94. 
95. Detect and record:
96. 
97. - AppHost project (`*.AppHost.csproj`), **or** a file-based AppHost — a bare
98.   `.cs` (commonly `apphost.cs`) with `#:sdk Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` /
99.   `#:package Aspire.Hosting.*` directives and a `DistributedApplication.CreateBuilder`
100.   call and no `.csproj`/`.sln` — and agent service projects
101. - Agent registrations (`AddAgent`, `ChatClientAgent`, `IChatClient` builders)
102. - Agent count, handoff edges, tool count per agent
103. - OTel wiring (`AddOpenTelemetry`, Aspire dashboard reference)
104. 
105. **Automated detection (large apps).** For the topology, OTel-coverage, and
106. model-assignment categories on a **larger codebase**, the deterministic detection
107. scripts save you from reading every source file by hand. **On a small app (a
108. handful of files), skip them and read the sources directly** — invoking them on a
109. tiny fixture costs more than it saves. When you do use them, invoke each as
110. `& "<skill-directory>/scripts/<Name>.ps1" -Path <app-root> -Json` and parse the
111. JSON:
112. 
113. - `Detect-Topology.ps1` — agent nodes, handoff edges, orphaned agents, per-file
114.   fan-out.
115. - `Detect-OtelCoverage.ps1` — presence of Aspire service defaults, the OTel SDK,
116.   an OTLP exporter, tracing/metrics builders, and `gen_ai.*` token telemetry.
117. - `Detect-ModelLiterals.ps1` — model-id literals and Foundry enum refs, split by
118.   AppHost vs service file, with a distinct-id count.
119. 
120. The scripts parse source text, so they also cover a file-based AppHost. They do
121. **detection only** — they never assign severity. Feed their output into the check
122. classes in step 2, then apply the evidence gate and severity rules yourself. If a
123. script errors or emits nothing, fall back to reading the reference doc and
124. scanning by hand (graceful degradation). See `references/detection-scripts.md`
125. for the exact contract.
126. 
127. If no agentic app is detected, abort and tell the user this skill does not
128. apply. Do not attempt to audit a non-agentic .NET project.
129. 
130. ### 2. Run the seven check classes
131. 
132. Evaluate the seven categories below and collect the confirmed findings; you will
133. present them in chat (step 5) and persist them to the report (step 4). **Do not
134. pre-read all seven reference docs** and **do not open an empty report file first**
135. — reason about the findings before you write anything. Open a category's
136. reference doc only to confirm a specific candidate finding.
137. 
138. | # | Category          | Reference                                  |
139. |---|-------------------|--------------------------------------------|
140. | 1 | Topology          | `references/topology-checks.md`            |
141. | 2 | Tool inventory    | `references/tool-inventory-checks.md`      |
142. | 3 | Message history   | `references/message-history-checks.md`     |
143. | 4 | Prompt weight     | `references/prompt-weight-checks.md`       |
144. | 5 | Parallelism       | `references/parallelism-checks.md`         |
145. | 6 | OTel coverage     | `references/otel-coverage-checks.md`       |
146. | 7 | Model assignment  | `references/model-assignment-checks.md`    |
147. 
148. For each check, record any findings with the schema in step 3.
149. 
150. Categories 1 (topology), 6 (OTel coverage), and 7 (model assignment) are seeded
151. by the detection scripts run in step 1 — read the parsed JSON, then confirm each
152. candidate against its reference doc. The remaining categories are evaluated by
153. inspecting the cited sources directly; consult their `references/` doc only when
154. a candidate finding needs confirmation.
155. 
156. ### 3. Finding schema
157. 
158. Every finding is a dict with these fields:
159. 
160. ```yaml
161. severity: critical | warn | info
162. check:    one of the slugs listed in references/check-glossary.md
163.           (e.g. model.same-default, history.full-share, otel.missing-sdk)
164. title:    short imperative phrase
165. file:     path relative to repo root
166. line:     1-based line number, or null
167. evidence: 1-3 line code snippet or measurement (must be present in the cited file)
168. why:      one paragraph explaining the impact
169. next:     concrete action the developer can take next
170. ref:      optional cross-skill route (e.g. "skill:configure-agentic-perf-rules")
171. ```
172. 
173. The `check` field is a dotted slug: `<category>.<descriptor>`. The
174. prefix before the dot encodes the category — there is no separate
175. `category` field. Category card (also rendered at the top of the
176. report's `## Findings` section):
177. 
178. | Category   | Coverage                | Reference                              |
179. |------------|-------------------------|----------------------------------------|
180. | `topology` | agent graph shape       | `references/topology-checks.md`        |
181. | `tools`    | per-agent tool list     | `references/tool-inventory-checks.md`  |
182. | `history`  | chat history strategy   | `references/message-history-checks.md` |
183. | `prompt`   | system prompt size/reuse| `references/prompt-weight-checks.md`   |
184. | `parallel` | concurrent invocations  | `references/parallelism-checks.md`     |
185. | `otel`     | instrumentation         | `references/otel-coverage-checks.md`   |
186. | `model`    | per-agent model id      | `references/model-assignment-checks.md`|
187. 
188. See `references/check-glossary.md` for the full slug→description table.
189. 
190. **Evidence gate** — before adding a finding to the report, re-open the
191. cited file and confirm the `evidence` snippet is present at or near
192. the cited line. Drop any finding that fails this check. Findings whose
193. evidence is "absence of X" must list the exact files and patterns
194. that were searched in the `evidence` field instead of a snippet.
195. 
196. Severity rules:
197. 
198. - **critical** — likely to break a user-visible flow, blow the token budget,
199.   or cause a cost spike. Always surfaced in chat.
200. - **warn** — measurable perf or cost regression, but app still works.
201. - **info** — observation worth knowing, no action required.
202. 
203. ### 4. Aggregate and write the report
204. 
205. Once you have the confirmed findings, sort them by severity (critical → warn →
206. info), then by `check` slug (stable lexical order so `history.*` < `model.*` <
207. `otel.*` < `parallel.*` < `prompt.*` < `tools.*` < `topology.*`) and write them
208. to the report with the `create` tool. This is a persisted copy of the analysis
209. you present in chat (step 5) — not the primary deliverable, but always written.
210. 
211. **Always write the report** — even for a read-only audit and even when
212. zero criticals are found (an empty-findings report is still worth persisting;
213. writing it is not a source edit). Write it to
214. `.copilot/perf-reports/scan.md` **relative to the scanned app's root** —
215. the directory that contains the solution / `*.AppHost.csproj`, or the
216. path the user pointed you at (e.g. auditing `./fixture` writes
217. `fixture/.copilot/perf-reports/scan.md`). Overwrite it on every run.
218. Git provides whatever history you want; the skill does
219. not maintain timestamped copies or `latest-*` mirrors. (Exception: when
220. a solution has multiple `*.AppHost.csproj` projects, write one report
221. per host as `scan-<host>.md` — see `references/common-pitfalls.md`.)
222. 
223. The category legend (one-liners describing what each prefix covers) is
224. inlined into the report itself — see `references/report-template.md`.
225. There is no separate glossary file. The slug encodes the check (e.g.
226. `history.full-share`, `topology.cycle`); readers don't need a lookup
227. table.
228. 
229. Create `.copilot/perf-reports/` if it does not exist.
230. 
231. This skill never touches `.gitignore`. If the user wants the report
232. ignored, recommend in chat that they add `.copilot/perf-reports/` to
233. their `.gitignore` themselves; do not edit it from this skill.
234. 
235. ### 5. Surface top findings in chat (required — this is your answer)
236. 
237. This step is the primary deliverable. Your final chat message **must** contain
238. the analysis, even after you have written `scan.md`. Print:
239. 
240. 1. Total counts (critical / warn / info).
241. 2. **The finding(s) in the user's stated concern category first** (e.g. topology
242.    when they said "too complex"), then the first up to 3 critical findings —
243.    each with title + `check` slug + file:line + next action.
244. 3. The full report path.
245. 4. If any findings have a `ref:` field, list the suggested follow-up skills.
246. 
247. Do not paste the entire report into chat, but never end with an empty or
248. one-line message — a saved file is not a substitute for answering the user.
249. 
250. ### 6. Offer to route into follow-up skills
251. 
252. After surfacing the top findings, **ask the user once** whether they
253. want to act on the routed follow-ups. The skill itself never edits
254. source — this step only routes into a sibling skill that owns its own
255. diff-and-confirm flow.
256. 
257. 1. Aggregate the unique `ref:` values across all findings.
258. 2. If the set is non-empty, print one prompt of the form:
259.    > Want me to follow up on any of these?
260.    > - **A.** Install/update perf rules via `configure-agentic-perf-rules` to enforce role-aware model selection on future code.
261.    > - **B.** Run `setup-maf-evals` to capture token/quality numbers.
262.    > - **C.** Run `configure-agentic-perf-rules` to install always-on rules.
263.    > - **D.** No — just leave the report.
264.    Render only the lettered options that correspond to refs actually
265.    present in the findings (skip letters whose target skill is not
266.    referenced).
267. 3. Wait for the user's response. If they pick a letter, hand off to the
268.    named skill with the audit report path as context. If they pick
269.    "no" or anything else, stop.
270. 4. Do **not** infer intent from the original audit-request prompt
271.    ("audit and fix it" is *intent* — the follow-up skill must still
272.    present its own diff and obtain its own confirmation before any
273.    write). This skill's job ends at the routing offer.
274. 
275. ### 7. Stop
276. 
277. This skill never edits source. If the user declined the offer in
278. step 6, or if there were no `ref:` fields in any finding, the skill
279. ends here.
280. 
281. ## Validation
282. 
283. After running:
284. 
285. - A file exists at `.copilot/perf-reports/scan.md` (overwritten if it
286.   was there before).
287. - The report has a `## Findings` section, even if empty (containing
288.   `_No findings._`).
289. - The summary counts in the report match the chat output.
290. 
291. ## Common pitfalls
292. 
293. - **Editing source code.** This skill is read-only. The ONLY write path
294.   it owns is `.copilot/perf-reports/scan.md`. Never edit `.gitignore`,
295.   source files, config files, or anything else. If a check tempts you
296.   to fix the issue inline, stop and add it as a finding instead.
297. - **Hallucinating findings.** Every finding must cite a real file and
298.   (where applicable) a real line. Before adding a finding to the
299.   report, re-open the cited file and verify the snippet exists at the
300.   cited line. If you cannot point to evidence, drop the finding.
